candidates.changed_node: root '*': CS_RANK(vol-normalized open-vs-21d-high distance) x CS_RANK($roe)
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_STD($open,10) from A (short-term open volatility) and TS_MAX($high,21) from B (the 21-day high reference). Fusion: B's raw, unscaled 'distance below the recent high' is dimensionless and comparable across low- and high-vol names once divided by A's own volatility normalizer -- a proper breakout/breakdown z-distance, which neither parent computes (B has no vol-scaling; A has no price-range concept). That normalized distance is then crossed with a fresh CS_RANK($roe), adding B's missing fundamental angle. Switched the price leg from B's $close to $open specifically to avoid reconstructing B's own 5-node '$close - TS_MAX(...)' subtree verbatim (checked: no archive member or Alpha101 formula pairs TS_MAX($high,21) with $open, or TS_STD($open,10) in any context, across all 8 run archives).

candidates.changed_node: root '-': TS_DELTA($roa,63) minus TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) from A and TS_DELTA($roa,63) from B, combined as a spread instead of either parent's own combinator (A multiplies two RANK legs; B subtracts two RANK legs from different fields). Interaction: is 63-day ROA improvement being arbitraged away faster in the most heavily-traded names, or does it show up more there -- a quality-momentum-vs-liquidity spread neither parent expresses (A has no fundamental; B has no liquidity conditioning). This also matches this archive's own validated pattern that a fundamental-minus-raw-leg spread carries signal. Note: $accrual_gap in B is only a 2-node leaf+rank and cannot supply the required 3-node donation, so the fusion necessarily runs through B's ROA-delta leg instead.

candidates.changed_node: root '*': TS_DELTA($roa,63) x ABS(TS_DELTA($open,1)), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_DELTA($roa,63) from A and TS_DELTA($open,1) from B, with B's leg wrapped in ABS to convert a raw directional tick into an event-magnitude leg (this archive's own record shows fundamentals pair with magnitude/vol legs, not signed displacement legs). Interaction: scales medium-term ROA improvement by the size of the stock's most recent one-day price shock, i.e. how much a quality-improving name is currently being repriced. Honest caveat: this is the weakest pair of the eight -- B's only donatable fragment is a single 1-day price tick, an inherently thin, noisy leg, so the fusion is real but thin.

candidates.changed_node: root '*': ABS(TS_DELTA($open,1)) x TS_RANK($dollar_volume,126), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_DELTA($open,1) from A (ABS-wrapped, magnitude not direction) and TS_RANK($dollar_volume,126) from B. Interaction: a genuine multi-horizon blend -- A's fast, contemporaneous price-shock magnitude conditioned by B's slow, 126-day liquidity percentile, rather than A's own raw same-day dollar volume or B's medium (10-day) price delta. A near-identical template, CS_RANK($roa) * TS_RANK($dollar_volume,126), is already a live archive member, confirming this shape clears the gates; the novelty here is substituting the price-shock-magnitude leg for the fundamental.

candidates.changed_node: root '*': TS_DELTA($open,10) x COUNT($accrual_gap<0,63), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_DELTA($open,10) from A and the $accrual_gap < 0 condition from B, re-windowed to 63 days (B's own 189-day COUNT wrapper can't be reused whole without oversharing). Interaction: weights 10-day price momentum by how often, over the last quarter, the stock has shown a negative accrual gap -- an earnings-quality red-flag frequency conditioning a pure price leg, which neither parent has alone (A carries no fundamental; B carries no price/momentum content).

candidates.changed_node: root '*': TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) x COUNT($accrual_gap<0,252), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63) from A and the $accrual_gap < 0 condition from B, re-windowed to 252 days (~1 year) instead of B's own 189. Interaction: a liquidity-percentile leg interacted with a roughly-annual frequency of negative-accrual quarters, flagging heavily-traded names with a persistent earnings-quality problem -- a liquidity-times-quality-risk screen neither parent expresses alone (A has no fundamental; B has no liquidity).

candidates.changed_node: root '-': COUNT($accrual_gap<0,21) minus TS_STD($return,21), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates the $accrual_gap < 0 condition from A, re-windowed to 21 days, and TS_STD($return,21) from B, combined as a spread rather than B's own guarded ratio. Interaction: matches this archive's validated pattern that a fundamental-leg-minus-raw-leg spread carries signal -- here, a one-month earnings-quality-flag frequency minus realized volatility, so a stock's recent volatility is judged relative to a fundamental red flag instead of in isolation.

candidates.changed_node: root '-': TS_MEAN($return,10) minus TS_STD($return,21), under one CS_RANK
candidates.rationale: Donates TS_STD($return,21) from A and TS_MEAN($return,10) from B, combined as a difference rather than either parent's own ratio/rank-spread. Interaction: a lower-confidence-bound-style risk-adjusted momentum score (expected 10-day return net of recent volatility) -- A has volatility with no return direction, B has return momentum (and a valuation leg) with no risk penalty; the child is the reward-per-unit-of-recent-risk measure neither parent computes. prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: CROSSOVER. Each pair below holds two parents from DIFFERENT archive
niches. Return one child per pair that genuinely combines them.

A child must keep a complete sub-expression of at least 3 nodes
from EACH parent, checked mechanically; a child that is really just one parent
with cosmetic changes is rejected. Put both parent ids in `parent_ids`.

In the rationale, state the fusion logic: what does the combination capture that
neither parent captures alone? A conditioning variable, a normaliser, an
interaction. If you cannot name one, the pair is a bad cross and you should say
so in the rationale rather than force it.
